content.rationale: Birth is where D12's creation — the change after the named dependencies, the file named by the change id the crossing reports, the summary — D22's refusal of an unresolvable --on set (naming each unknown id, before anything is created), the flag grammar (the summary-less and unnameable-argument refusals, and order-free recognition), N6's placeholder skeleton, O6's one-line report, S3-new's mechanism, S3-new-position's refusal of an ambiguous --on set (naming each tied id before anything is created), and S5-lifecycle's bracketing meet; this check drives the handler over a scratch jj workspace whose node files are named by real change ids, and pins each of those, plus that the handler is the table's shape — a `Verb` row for it compiles (M-route). It reaches store_load and store_write, so it is a crate of its own. I1-serde (`orrvsxqq`) fixes the JSON layer the crate is written against — serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive, and I1-schema (`zmmyomyp`) fixes the validator these documents are checked with. It also pins the refusal site (S2-write-refusal-site, myoztqyu): with the workspace's nodes/ absent, the write cannot be completed, so birth refuses, naming the cause. It pins S5-birth-fail (kvwonkzy) too: with the workspace's nodes/ read-only the write cannot complete, so the birth refuses, naming the cause, and the change it opened is abandoned — the repo's change count and heads are back to what they were before the invocation. It pins the read's refusal site (S2-read-refusal-site, vollyzvn): a --on target whose document cannot be read refuses before birth, naming it.
